reason: E3 directly supports the role of edge dislocations in high-temperature strength retention for specific refractory HEAs, but none of the cited evidence demonstrates a temperature-induced transition from screw to edge dislocation control, which is the core mechanistic premise. E1 and E2 discuss dislocation slip and deformation but do not identify dislocation character or a transition mechanism.
premises: Plastic flow in BCC elemental metals and dilute alloys is generally controlled by screw dislocations
In some refractory HEAs, edge dislocations can be responsible for high strength and strength retention at high temperatures
A temperature-induced transition from screw-dominated to edge-dominated dislocation mechanism occurs in refractory HEAs
This transition enhances plastic flow and supports high yield strength retention at elevated temperatures
The transition can be observed via increased prevalence of edge dislocations in microstructural analyses at high temperatures
